description:
=== DONE (s473t5d) ===
FOUND + FIXED s473t5d (Opus, 2026-09-13) by #1501 round 5.

t/io/closepid.t produced NO TAP AT ALL:

  Error while parsing arguments to defmacro p-open:
    too many elements in ($fh1 "-|" $perl "-e" "sleep 50")
    to satisfy lambda list (fh mode &optional filename):
    between 2 and 3 expected, but got 5

`p-open` was `(fh mode &optional filename)`, so perl's documented LIST form --
`open($fh, "-|", $prog, @argv)`, which execs PROG DIRECTLY with no shell -- was
a COMPILE-TIME failure, not a runtime one: the form never ran.

The fix is small because the machinery was already there (rule 11):
`%p-open-fork-pipe` already takes `cmd-args` as a LIST and does
`(apply #'p-exec cmd-args)`, and `p-exec` with more than one string is already
the no-shell exec.  So: `p-open` gains `&rest more`, `%p-open-impl` gains a
`more-args` parameter, and the pipe arm conses the extra args onto the command.

RULE 12: a second target on a NON-pipe mode is perl's FATAL
"More than one argument to open(,':perlio')" (probed), so `%p-open-impl` dies
naming the mode rather than picking one.  PCL's text names the mode the program
wrote (`More than one argument to open(,'>')`); the exact layer spelling is not
a goal (project_error_message_fidelity_not_required).

PROBED 5.40.3, nine shapes: the read pipe passes @ARGV through; a shell
metacharacter in an argument survives LITERALLY (`'a;echo BOOM'` arrives as
that string -- a shell would have run it); the write pipe works; a one-element
list is still no shell.

RESULT: t/io/closepid.t 0/0 DIFF -> 3/0 OK (its 1 blessed row and 3 shortfall
rows left the baselines by EDIT).  Guard Pl/t/open-modes-01.t rows 4+5.
No emission change (the compiler was already emitting all five arguments).
subject: the LIST form of a pipe open -- open($fh,"-|",$prog,@argv), perl's no-shell spelling -- was a macroexpansion ARITY ERROR that killed the whole top-level form
